name: Hothir
overview: Hothir was a male Levite set apart for prophetic ministry through music, specifically with lyres, harps, and cymbals. He was the son of Heman and was chosen as the twenty-first singer by lot among the musicians dedicated to worship. His role highlights his involvement in the organized temple music ministry during the time recorded in 1 Chronicles.
namesAndTitles: The name Hothir means "one who remains," reflecting a proper name without indication of divine origin. This meaning may suggest endurance or permanence, but the biblical text simply records it as his given name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hothir as the son of Heman, linking him to a prominent Levitical family known for musical service. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Hothir's significance lies in his role as a Levite musician chosen by lot to prophesy through instrumental worship, demonstrating the ordered and Spirit-led nature of temple service. Being the twenty-first chosen singer among the descendants of Heman underscores his part in the sacred musical ministry that accompanied prophecy and praise in Israel. His service contributes to the biblical portrayal of worship as a divinely appointed and spiritually powerful act.
